partB: Which nuclear enzyme normally produces the mammalian primary precursor containing 18S, 5.8S and 28S rRNA sequences?
Pol I transcribes the large rDNA precursor. Pol III makes 5S rRNA separately; Pol II makes the mRNAs for ribosomal proteins, not this precursor.
Which pairing is incorrect in a conventional mammalian nuclear system?
5S rRNA is normally a Pol III product. Its residence in the large ribosomal subunit does not make its transcriptional origin the same as 28S rRNA.
Which RNA shows that Pol II products are not restricted to mRNA?
U1 is a representative Pol II-transcribed noncoding RNA. U6 is a contrasting Pol III snRNA; the other listed products normally use Pol I or III.
Which statement correctly distinguishes TBP from TFIID?
TFIID is a subunit of TBP
TBP is a component of a larger TFIID complex
TBP is the catalytic subunit of Pol II
TFIID includes TBP and associated TAFs. TBP itself can also participate in distinct Pol I and Pol III factors; it is not a polymerase subunit.
Which property of a conventional TATA element is most accurate?
It is required in all Pol II promoters
It provides one possible upstream recognition site
It must overlap the translation start codon
It uniquely identifies Pol II genes
A TATA box is one possible core promoter element, not universal. Some Pol III promoters also contain TATA motifs, and transcription start and translation start are distinct.
A typical initiator (Inr) element is located where?
The Inr encompasses the transcription start region. Downstream and upstream promoter elements may cooperate with it.
Which factor has the most direct textbook association with positioning Pol II relative to the TBP-promoter scaffold?
TFIIB connects the Pol II machinery to the promoter-associated scaffold and contributes to start-site selection. TFIIIA and TFIIIC are Pol III factors; RRN3 acts with Pol I.
Which factor associates closely with Pol II during its recruitment into the preinitiation complex?
TFIIF associates with Pol II and assists productive recruitment. SL1 and UBF organize Pol I transcription, whereas TFIIIA recognizes the 5S internal control region.
Which factor helps recruit and organize TFIIH in the Pol II initiation apparatus?
TFIIE supports association and organization of TFIIH. The remaining factors are associated with other nuclear transcription systems.
Which pair of activities is associated with TFIIH in standard mammalian Pol II initiation?
XPB-dependent DNA translocation and CDK7-mediated phosphorylation
XPB contributes ATP-dependent promoter opening and CDK7 phosphorylates the CTD. Neither activity is the core phosphodiester-forming reaction of Pol II.
Which CTD repeat is the canonical heptapeptide?
The canonical protein sequence is Tyr-Ser-Pro-Thr-Ser-Pro-Ser. TATA and AUG are nucleic acid motifs, not the CTD amino acid sequence.
Early Pol II Ser5 phosphorylation is particularly associated with which downstream process?
Ser5 phosphorylation contributes to recruitment of capping factors. It does not itself transfer the guanosine cap or perform the other processes.
Which set belongs to the representative mammalian Pol I initiation apparatus?
UBF, SL1 and RRN3 support Pol I initiation. The first set describes Pol III 5S machinery; the third is Pol II; the fourth mixes bacterial transcription and replication components.
Which factor specifically helps recognize the internal control region of a canonical 5S rRNA gene?
TFIIIA helps recruit TFIIIC at the 5S gene. TFIIA and TFIIE are Pol II general factors; CDK7 is a kinase.
Which promoter class is typically associated with internal A and B boxes?
Canonical tRNA type 2 promoters use internal A and B boxes recognized by TFIIIC. U6 is a representative upstream type 3 promoter.
Which statement about mammalian U6 transcription is correct?
It necessarily uses the Pol I large rRNA precursor promoter
It is always transcribed by Pol II because it participates in splicing
It requires TFIIIA for internal A and B boxes
It exemplifies a Pol III promoter using upstream recognition elements
U6 commonly uses upstream elements, SNAPc and a Brf2-containing TFIIIB. Its function in splicing does not determine polymerase identity.
Which factor contains TBP in conventional Pol III machinery?
TFIIIB contains TBP and other Pol III-associated factors. TFIIB is a separate Pol II factor and should not be confused with TFIIIB.
In many animal nuclear extracts, which relative alpha-amanitin response is expected?
Pol I highly sensitive; Pol II resistant
Pol II highly sensitive; Pol III sensitive at higher concentrations; Pol I relatively resistant
Pol III resistant at all doses in all organisms
This is the conventional comparative response under specified conditions. Absolute concentrations and sensitivity patterns are not universal across species and assay designs.
A nuclear polymerase's integral subunits should be counted separately from what?
General factors are interacting components of the initiation apparatus, not automatically permanent subunits of the core enzyme. The other choices belong to the enzyme itself.
A 47S precursor contains several rRNA sequences. What does S denote?
A sum of mature rRNA lengths
Svedberg units describe sedimentation behavior. Sedimentation coefficients are not simply additive masses or sequence lengths.
Assertion: Loss of TBP can compromise more than one nuclear transcription system. Reason: TBP is a component of TFIID, SL1 and TFIIIB.
Both true; reason does not explain assertion
Shared TBP helps explain why its loss can affect several systems, unlike disruption of a class-specific partner.
Assertion: Every Pol II promoter must possess a classical TATA box. Reason: TBP can bind and bend suitable TATA-containing DNA.
Both true; reason does not explain assertion
TBP recognition of TATA is real, but many promoters lack a classical TATA box and use alternative recognition arrangements.
Assertion: Some Pol III control elements can be copied into the RNA. Reason: Canonical tRNA genes use internal A and B boxes.
Both true; reason does not explain assertion
The internal elements lie downstream of the start and can contribute both to DNA recognition and to the RNA sequence.
Assertion: Ser5 phosphorylation itself chemically adds the 5′ cap to RNA. Reason: Ser5-phosphorylated CTD can recruit capping machinery.
Both true; reason does not explain assertion
Phosphorylation recruits or helps coordinate other enzymes; those enzymes perform capping chemistry.
Assertion: Normal promoter occupancy does not ensure normal RNA output. Reason: Bound complexes can fail to open DNA or progress into productive synthesis.
Both true; reason does not explain assertion
Occupancy is a state measurement, while RNA synthesis is a flux. The stated downstream block explains the distinction.
Evaluate: I. Pol II CTD is a repeat-rich region of RPB1. II. Pol III transcribes all snRNAs. III. TFIIH has functions in DNA repair. IV. Pol I normally makes 5S rRNA.
I and III are correct. U1 and U2 are representative Pol II snRNAs, and 5S is normally a Pol III product.
Evaluate: I. TFIID contains TBP. II. TFIIF is a major cap-transfer enzyme. III. TFIIE contributes to TFIIH recruitment. IV. TFIIIA recognizes canonical 5S promoter DNA.
I, III and IV describe the initiation machinery. TFIIF does not catalyze cap transfer.
Match 1. TFIIIA, 2. UBF, 3. TFIIB, 4. XPB to a. promoter opening motor, b. 5S internal recognition, c. Pol I rDNA organization, d. Pol II positioning.
TFIIIA is associated with 5S recognition, UBF with rDNA architecture, TFIIB with Pol II positioning, and XPB with ATP-dependent opening.
Match 1. Pol I, 2. Pol II, 3. Pol III to representative products a. tRNA, b. major pre-rRNA, c. pre-mRNA.
The major rRNA precursor is made by Pol I, protein-coding primary transcripts by Pol II, and nuclear tRNAs by Pol III.

Which statements describe the limitations of the three-polymerase classification? I. Mitochondrial transcription uses distinct machinery. II. Some plants possess additional nuclear polymerases. III. All cellular rRNAs are synthesized by nuclear Pol I.
The three major nuclear classes do not exhaust organelle or specialized plant transcription. Even conventional nuclear 5S rRNA contradicts III.
partC: experimental
A promoter mutant retains TBP binding but loses Pol II occupancy; purified Pol II copies an artificial exposed template normally. Which inference is strongest?
The catalytic center must be destroyed
The defect is consistent with recruitment or stabilization after initial recognition
The mature RNA is necessarily unstable
The ribosomal subunit is defective

The positive binding and artificial-template controls separate TBP recognition and core catalysis from promoter-directed assembly. The result does not identify one exact recruitment protein without further tests.
experimental
Pol II and all general factors occupy a promoter, but a DNA-opening assay is negative. An artificial pre-opened template restores initial RNA synthesis. Which step is most directly implicated?
RNA export
Pol III internal promoter recognition
RNA capping
Promoter opening
Bypassing the opening barrier restores initial catalysis, implicating opening rather than export or capping. XPB function is a candidate, not conclusively the only defective component.
experimental
A TFIIH mutant shows normal promoter opening and impaired early CTD Ser5 phosphorylation. Which activity should be examined first?
CDK7 kinase
TFIIIA recognition
Ribosomal RNA cleavage
XPB translocation alone
CDK7 directly contributes to the missing early CTD modification. Normal opening argues against a primary motor defect under the tested conditions; assay complex integrity too.
experimental
Removing TFIIIA from a defined system sharply reduces 5S RNA synthesis but leaves canonical tRNA transcription unchanged. Which addition is most informative?
Ribosomal protein
Extra dNTPs
Purified functional TFIIIA
DNA ligase
Add-back of the specifically depleted factor tests whether its loss caused the selective defect. A ribosomal protein would not restore the promoter recognition step.
experimental
In a representative animal system, loss of TFIIIC affects both 5S and tRNA templates, but U6 transcription remains high. What is the best explanation?
U6 is always a Pol II transcript
U6 can use a distinct upstream recognition pathway to recruit TFIIIB
All three templates require TFIIIA equally
The three enzymes are identical
The result fits the type 3 promoter architecture. It does not require changing the assigned polymerase for U6.
experimental
A CTD-truncated Pol II preparation retains nucleotide incorporation on an artificial template, but nascent cellular RNA is recovered poorly by a cap-specific assay. What conclusion is justified?
The mutation must remove the DNA template
All RNA synthesis must be absent
The CTD is itself the cap-transfer enzyme
A processing-coupling defect is plausible; compare nascent synthesis and recovery controls

Artificial-template activity supports retained catalytic competence under that condition. The cellular result suggests altered coupling but requires controls for transcript abundance, cap recovery and RNA stability.
experimental
A promoter insertion leaves TBP occupancy unchanged but moves the dominant RNA start site. Which measurement is most directly relevant?
Primary transcript 5′ end mapping
Protein mass only
Total genomic DNA copy number only
Ribosome sedimentation only
Mapping primary starts distinguishes changed positioning from altered transcript abundance. It must exclude misleading processed or degraded ends.
experimental
A high-dose inhibitor reduces both 5S and pre-mRNA synthesis acutely, while major pre-rRNA synthesis is largely unchanged. In a calibrated mammalian system, which interpretation fits?
Pol I only inhibited
DNA replication only inhibited
Pol II and Pol III inhibited more than Pol I
All three equally inhibited
This fits the characteristic high-concentration alpha-amanitin pattern. The conclusion is context dependent and strongest with nascent synthesis controls.
experimental
After hours of selective Pol II inhibition, pre-rRNA production also declines. What additional test best addresses whether the drug directly inhibits Pol I?
Measure only total protein after 24 hours
Assay purified Pol I acutely with matched inhibitor conditions
Measure only cell size
Sequence a random tRNA
Purified Pol I tests direct enzyme sensitivity without most secondary cellular effects. A long treatment alone cannot distinguish direct inhibition from loss of Pol II-dependent proteins.
experimental
Species A and B Pol I systems work with their own rDNA promoters but fail on reciprocal promoters. Which conclusion is most defensible?
Their RNA backbones use different chemical bonds
All polymerase I subunits must be unrelated
Both promoters must lack DNA
Promoter recognition or recruitment compatibility differs; component swaps could localize the determinant
Cross-species incompatibility can arise from coevolved interfaces despite conserved chemistry. Homologous controls demonstrate that each preparation is active.
experimental
A tRNA B-box mutation lowers precursor synthesis and changes a nucleotide in the mature tRNA. Which design separates the two possible defects?
Measure precursor synthesis and independently assess the resulting RNA's function
Measure only total ATP
Delete every tRNA gene
Measure only Pol II CTD phosphorylation
An internal control sequence can affect promoter recognition and product function independently. Separate transcription and mature-RNA assays resolve the two effects.
experimental
An antibody against Ser5-phosphorylated CTD gives half the signal in a CTD truncation mutant. Which interpretation is safest?
Each remaining site must be exactly half as phosphorylated
The mutant must lack all Pol II
The signal may reflect fewer epitopes or changed enzyme abundance as well as modification
The antibody directly measures transcription initiation rate
An epitope count and protein abundance affect signal. Normalize against an invariant Pol II region and account for repeat number before interpreting per-site phosphorylation.
experimental
Reconstitution with TBP alone restores transcription on a TATA template but not a TATA-less template; intact TFIID restores both. What does this support?
The TATA-less template is not DNA
TAF-mediated functions are important for the second template under these conditions
Pol III must transcribe all TATA-less genes
TBP is the RNA polymerase
The differential rescue supports a role for additional TFIID components. It does not identify the exact TAF or imply a universal dependence for all TATA-less promoters.
experimental
An assembly-defective TFIIF mutant reduces Pol II recruitment. Adding more TFIIH fails to rescue the defect. Which reasoning is sound?
TFIIH must be absent in the original reaction
The promoter is necessarily a Pol III gene
Extra opening machinery does not necessarily repair a missing recruitment interaction
RNA processing is the sole explanation
The block may precede recruitment of the opening apparatus. A rescue with competent TFIIF and a direct occupancy assay would test the hypothesis.
experimental
A selective TFIIA perturbation reduces transcription modestly in a minimal naked-DNA assay but strongly in cells. Which conclusion is justified?
TFIIA cannot function in cells
The assay demonstrates an impossible result
TFIIA is a nucleotide substrate
Its contribution can depend on competing interactions and assembly context
A favorable purified template can reduce the need for stabilizing functions. The different magnitude does not establish that TFIIA changes its molecular identity.
experimental
A ChIP-like binding assay detects TBP at a locus but no transcript-specific information is available. Which additional result would best identify its polymerase?
The locus is rich in adenine alone
Enzyme-specific occupancy together with nascent RNA identity
Total cell DNA content
The presence of a nucleus alone
TBP is shared among nuclear systems, so its occupancy is not diagnostic. Class-specific enzyme evidence and transcript identity strengthen assignment.
numerical
An unprocessed 160-nucleotide RNA is initiated de novo. How many phosphodiester linkages and polymerization-associated PPi molecules are formed?
80 and 80
A linear chain of n residues has n−1 internucleotide linkages. The first nucleotide retains its 5′ triphosphate; the remaining 159 additions release PPi.
numerical
A hypothetical promoter-binding protein has Kd = 30 nM. At free protein 60 nM, what is site occupancy in the independent one-site equilibrium model?
θ = p/(Kd+p) = 60/(30+60) = 2/3, dimensionless. A binding fraction cannot exceed one.
numerical
Twelve equivalent promoters each have occupancy 0.25 and effective productive initiation rate 0.4 min⁻¹ per occupied promoter. What is total mean flux?
4.8/min
0.1/min
12/min
1.2/min
J = Nfk = 12×0.25×0.4 = 1.2 events/min. The model assumes comparable independent copies and stable averages.
numerical

An idealized crude extract gives 180 units without inhibitor, 100 at a low dose eliminating only Pol II, and 35 at a high dose eliminating Pol II and III. What are Pol I, II and III activity contributions?
Pol I = 35; Pol II = 180−100 = 80; Pol III = 100−35 = 65. These are assay activities, not enzyme molecule counts.
numerical
Fraction A falls from 150 to 45 units/min after inhibitor. Fraction B falls from 40 to 20. Which has higher percentage inhibition?
Both 50%
A loses 105/150 = 70%; B loses 20/40 = 50%. The smaller absolute treated activity of B does not mean greater relative inhibition.
numerical
A hypothetical CTD has 32 perfect YSPTSPS repeats. How many residues and potential Ser5 positions occur in those repeats?
96 and 32
32×7 = 224 residues. There is exactly one Ser5 position per canonical repeat; all serine positions together would total 96.
numerical
A nucleus has 150 active rDNA units, each producing 0.6 precursors/min. Processing succeeds for 80% of precursors, yielding one set of three major rRNAs each. How many sets/min?
150×0.6 = 90 precursors/min; 90×0.8 = 72 complete sets/min. Counting individual rRNAs would give 216, not 216 sets.
numerical
A mutant synthesizes an RNA at 80 molecules/hour with first-order degradation constant 0.2/hour. Under the simple one-pool steady-state model, what abundance is predicted?
16 molecules
400 molecules
80 molecules
0.0025 molecules
At steady state s = dR, so R = 80/0.2 = 400 molecules. This does not measure transcription rate without knowing degradation.
integrative

A growing cell obtains 70 complete sets of major rRNAs, 120 copies of 5S, and enough ribosomal proteins for 85 ribosomes in a time interval. With no surplus and ideal assembly, which pathway's output limits assembly?
Pol III, because 5S is in the large subunit
Pol II, because proteins are required
Pol I-derived major rRNA sets, limiting output to 70
No pathway, because 70+120+85=275
Assembly requires one of each specified set, so the minimum is 70. The sum is not a ribosome count, and the other supplies are in excess in this model.
